subject: social_science
chapter_title: Civilising the Native, Educating the Nation

concepts.title: The Tradition of Orientalism
concepts.definition: A scholarly approach by British officials like William Jones who respected ancient Indian heritage and promoted the study of Sanskrit and Persian.
concepts.key_idea: Respecting and reviving ancient Indian texts to understand and govern the country.
question_patterns: Who was William Jones and what were his interests?
Define the term Orientalists in the context of British India.
What was the purpose of the Asiatic Society of Bengal?
Why did Jones and Colebrooke respect ancient Indian culture?
Explain the attitude of Orientalists towards Indian civilization.

solution_steps.explain: William Jones, Henry Colebrooke, and Nathaniel Halhed were key Orientalists.
They aimed to discover, translate, and study ancient Indian sacred and legal texts.

concepts.title: Early Orientalist Institutions
concepts.definition: Educational centers established by the British to encourage traditional Indian learning in Arabic, Persian, and Sanskrit.
concepts.key_idea: Setting up colleges to win the hearts of subjects by teaching familiar subjects.
question_patterns: When and why was the Calcutta Madrasa set up?
What was the objective of the Hindu College in Benaras?
Identify the year the Hindu College was established in Benaras.
Which languages were promoted by the Calcutta Madrasa?
How did the British hope to win the respect of Indian subjects through education?

solution_steps.explain: Calcutta Madrasa (1781) and Hindu College Benaras (1791).
Arabic, Persian, Islamic law, and ancient Sanskrit texts.

concepts.title: Anglicist Critique of Orientalism
concepts.definition: The viewpoint held by officials like James Mill and Thomas Macaulay who dismissed Eastern knowledge as unscientific and non-serious.
concepts.key_idea: Promoting useful and practical Western knowledge over Eastern literature.
question_patterns: Why did James Mill attack the Orientalists?
What did Macaulay mean by his single shelf of a good European library quote?
How did critics describe Eastern literature and thought?
What was the main aim of education according to James Mill?
Contrast the views of Orientalists and their critics.

solution_steps.explain: James Mill and Thomas Babington Macaulay were the primary critics.
They argued Eastern knowledge was full of errors and lacked practical utility.

concepts.title: English Education Act of 1835
concepts.definition: A legislative decision to make English the medium of instruction for higher education in India and stop promoting Oriental institutions.
concepts.key_idea: Institutionalizing English as the primary language for Indian education.
question_patterns: What were the main provisions of the English Education Act of 1835?
Which language became the medium of instruction for higher education in 1835?
How did the 1835 Act affect Oriental institutions like the Calcutta Madrasa?
What was the significance of Macaulay's Minute?
How did the British view Oriental institutions after 1835?

solution_steps.explain: English was chosen as the medium for higher education.
Promotion of Madrasas and Sanskrit colleges was halted.

concepts.title: Wood's Despatch of 1854
concepts.definition: An educational policy document sent by Charles Wood that emphasized the economic and moral benefits of European learning.
concepts.key_idea: Aligning Indian education with British commercial interests and administrative needs.
question_patterns: What was Wood's Despatch and who issued it?
How would European learning benefit trade and commerce according to the Despatch?
What moral improvements did the British expect from European education?
List the measures introduced following the 1854 Despatch.
Why did the British want to create a demand for British goods through education?

solution_steps.explain: European learning would help Indians recognize the advantages of trade expansion.
It aimed to produce honest civil servants for the Company.

concepts.title: Pathshala Student Estimation
concepts.definition: A calculation of the total student population in Bengal and Bihar based on the number of local schools and average attendance reported by William Adam.
concepts.key_idea: Quantifying the reach of the flexible vernacular education system in the 1830s.
question_patterns: Calculate the total number of children in pathshalas if there are 100000 schools with 20 students each.
How many students were being taught in Bengal and Bihar according to Adam's report?
If a district has 500 pathshalas with 20 students each, find the total students.
What is the total student count for 1 lakh schools with an average of 20 pupils?
Find the total children in vernacular schools based on Adam's data.

solution_steps.explain: The number of pathshalas is school_count.
Multiply the number of schools by the average students per school.

concepts.title: Pre-British Vernacular Education
concepts.definition: The flexible system of pathshalas characterized by oral teaching, lack of fixed infrastructure, and schedules adapted to the harvest cycle.
concepts.key_idea: A decentralized education system tailored to the needs of the local community and peasant families.
question_patterns: Describe the flexible features of the pathshala system.
Why were classes not held during harvest time in pathshalas?
How was the fee structure determined in local schools?
What were the teaching methods used by gurus in the 1830s?
List three things associated with modern schools that were absent in pathshalas.

solution_steps.explain: No fixed fees, buildings, or timetables; classes paused during harvests.
Teaching was oral and adapted to the level of individual students.

concepts.title: Post-1854 Pathshala Reforms
concepts.definition: The imposition of government control over vernacular schools through regular inspections, textbooks, and standardized examinations.
concepts.key_idea: Transforming flexible local schools into a disciplined, state-regulated system.
question_patterns: What changes did the Company introduce in pathshalas after 1854?
Who were government pandits and what was their role?
How did the new rules of discipline affect children from poor families?
What happened to pathshalas that did not accept government rules?
Explain the impact of annual examinations on the vernacular system.

solution_steps.explain: Introduction of textbooks, timetables, and regular fees.
Appointment of government pandits to oversee groups of schools.

concepts.title: Mahatma Gandhi's Educational Philosophy
concepts.definition: A vision of education that rejected English as the medium, focusing instead on dignity, self-respect, and the development of the mind through handicrafts.
concepts.key_idea: Education should be in the mother tongue and focus on practical skills and character building.
question_patterns: Why did Mahatma Gandhi argue that English education enslaved Indians?
What did Gandhi mean by literacy is not the end of education?
Why did Gandhi emphasize learning a handicraft?
How did Western education create a sense of inferiority according to Gandhi?
What was Gandhi's view on the medium of instruction?

solution_steps.explain: Gandhi believed English education distanced Indians from their own culture.
He proposed teaching useful crafts to develop the mind and soul.

concepts.title: Tagore's Santiniketan
concepts.definition: An educational institution founded by Rabindranath Tagore to foster creative learning in a natural environment, free from rigid discipline.
concepts.key_idea: Combining the best of Indian tradition with Western science in a natural setting.
question_patterns: Why did Rabindranath Tagore establish Santiniketan?
How did Tagore's childhood experience shape his views on school?
What did Tagore mean by 'abode of peace'?
Contrast Tagore's and Gandhi's views on Western civilization.
What subjects did Tagore emphasize at Santiniketan?

solution_steps.explain: The school was set in a rural area to allow children to live in harmony with nature.
It combined art, music, and dance with modern science and technology.

worked_examples.question_pattern: According to Adam's report, if there were {school_count} pathshalas and each had {students_per_school} students, what was the total number of children being taught?

solution_template.explain: Multiply 100000 schools by 20 students per school.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Find the total student population in a region with {school_count} schools and {students_per_school} students per school.

solution_template.explain: Multiply 50000 schools by 15 students per school.

questions: Match the following: William Jones, Rabindranath Tagore, Thomas Macaulay, Mahatma Gandhi, Pathshalas.
State whether true or false: James Mill was a severe critic of the Orientalists.
State whether true or false: The 1854 Despatch on education was in favour of English being introduced as a medium of higher education in India.
Why did William Jones feel the need to study Indian history, philosophy and law?
Why did James Mill and Thomas Macaulay think that European education was essential in India?
Why did Mahatma Gandhi want to teach children handicrafts?
Why did Mahatma Gandhi think that English education had enslaved Indians?
